lessons.text: Docstring-walk gates must assert an object's own __doc__ (or __dict__ doc), never inspect.getdoc: Python 3.12+ getdoc inherits docstrings from documented non-object bases (Enum), so removing a subclass's own class docstring passes the gate.

lessons.text: When a task audits 'every module has a //! contract', enumerate modules from the filesystem (all src/**/*.rs), not from the design's layer table — top-level modules outside the table (error.rs, result.rs) were missed.

lessons.key: ac_gap::when a metadata sidecar is resolved at the pom lang layer and consumed at the codegen layer attributes attached to pom nodes that do not surface in codegen s runtime catalogs e g a var shadowed never assigned so the kernel omits it from opvar names must be cross checked at the codegen boundary silently dropping the orphan metadata violates fail loud
lessons.text: When a metadata sidecar is resolved at the POM/lang layer and consumed at the codegen layer, attributes attached to POM nodes that do not surface in codegen's runtime catalogs (e.g. a var shadowed/never-assigned so the kernel omits it from opvar_names) must be cross-checked at the codegen boundary — silently dropping the orphan metadata violates fail-loud.
evidence: .specs/features/phdl-introspection-attributes/validation.md Edge Cases bullet 3 (orphan @unit/@description on shadowed var); pom/design.rs:469-500; device/mod.rs:428-440 (piperine-lang/pom, piperine-codegen/device, fail-loud)

lessons.text: Before writing 'delete the unenforceable rule' into a spec, check whether the rule is unreachable or merely unenforced — an unenforced-but-reachable rule needs its status stated in place, since deleting it trades documentation drift for a silent capability regression.

lessons.key: ac_gap::never plan against a quoted test count grep the tree for test and reconcile against the runner s number because a cfg any file contributes tests to the source count and zero to the gate
lessons.text: Never plan against a quoted test count: grep the tree for #[test] and reconcile against the runner's number, because a #![cfg(any())] file contributes tests to the source count and zero to the gate.

lessons.key: spec_deviation::when one task s dispatcher must call into a sibling module the compiler requires to compile as a whole unit ship that module s real implementation in the dispatcher s commit instead of a stub and record it as a spec deviation rather than forcing an artificial per task stub boundary
lessons.text: When one task's dispatcher must call into a sibling module the compiler requires to compile as a whole unit, ship that module's real implementation in the dispatcher's commit instead of a stub, and record it as a SPEC_DEVIATION rather than forcing an artificial per-task stub boundary.

lessons.key: spec_deviation::when an importance sampling or distribution shift estimator only shifts one distribution family e g gauss with resolvable sigma state the narrowed scope in the type s own doc comment and keep every other distribution unbiased but unshifted likelihood ratio 1 rather than silently approximating or blocking on full multivariate support
lessons.text: When an importance-sampling or distribution-shift estimator only shifts one distribution family (e.g. gauss with resolvable sigma), state the narrowed scope in the type's own doc comment and keep every other distribution unbiased-but-unshifted (likelihood ratio 1), rather than silently approximating or blocking on full multivariate support.

lessons.key: surviving_mutant::a settled only post event fixture must use a net whose value at the mutated wrong dispatch point genuinely differs from its correct value an initial equals final glitch fixture cannot discriminate stale vs settled dispatch
lessons.text: A settled-only/post-event fixture must use a net whose value at the mutated (wrong) dispatch point genuinely differs from its correct value — an initial-equals-final glitch fixture cannot discriminate stale-vs-settled dispatch.
evidence: crates/piperine-solver/tests/digital_settle_subscriber.rs (mutation: dispatch pre-settle snapshot instead of post-settle) (test-design)

lessons.text: A CSE/dedup claim (collapses to one call) needs an assertion that counts the actual emitted call or instruction sites, not just a numeric result that would be identical whether dedup ran once or twice.

lessons.key: spec_precision_gap::when a tn task ships a docs rewrite roadmap spec and later commits fix a b retire triple close items the docs already described as open the docs must be re synced in the same commit or the next docs commit otherwise the traceability table and roadmap contradict the measured state
lessons.text: When a Tn task ships a docs rewrite (ROADMAP/spec) and later commits (Fix A/B, retire-triple) close items the docs already described as open, the docs MUST be re-synced in the same commit or the next docs commit — otherwise the traceability table and ROADMAP contradict the measured state.

lessons.key: spec_precision_gap::when a spec ac names a specific test harness e g an existing tolerancecontract and the implementer must substitute a lower level equivalent because the named harness s dependency chain is broken mid feature add a follow up task to swap back to the real harness once the blocker clears don t leave the substitution permanent without revisiting it
lessons.text: When a spec AC names a specific test harness (e.g. an existing ToleranceContract), and the implementer must substitute a lower-level equivalent because the named harness's dependency chain is broken mid-feature, add a follow-up task to swap back to the real harness once the blocker clears — don't leave the substitution permanent without revisiting it.

lessons.key: spec_deviation::when a retarget task documents a list of test files broken by the change verify the list by actually running every target in the crate not just the ones that fail to compile a target that compiles but fails at runtime on stale fixture syntax is invisible to a compile error scan and will be silently undercounted
lessons.text: When a retarget task documents a list of test files broken by the change, verify the list by actually running every target in the crate (not just the ones that fail to compile) — a target that compiles but fails at runtime on stale fixture syntax is invisible to a compile-error scan and will be silently undercounted.

lessons.key: gate_fail::a gate level defined in tasks md as a literal command e g full cargo test workspace must be re validated as actually runnable before the feature is marked closed don t let per task deferred see progress log entries accumulate across dozens of tasks without a dedicated closing task that either fixes the command or formally re scopes the gate definition
lessons.text: A gate level defined in tasks.md as a literal command (e.g. 'full' = cargo test --workspace) must be re-validated as actually runnable before the feature is marked closed — don't let per-task '~ deferred, see progress log' entries accumulate across dozens of tasks without a dedicated closing task that either fixes the command or formally re-scopes the gate definition.
evidence: cargo test --workspace (does not compile at feature close: piperine-lang tests/elab.rs, 25 errors) (process)

lessons.key: ac_gap::when an open item s own text says a follow up task must be added before a phase closes add a checklist gate at that phase s close out task that fails loud if the follow up was never created an open item stated as a hard requirement is not self enforcing just because it was written down
lessons.text: When an open item's own text says a follow-up task MUST be added before a phase closes, add a checklist gate at that phase's close-out task that fails loud if the follow-up was never created — an open item stated as a hard requirement is not self-enforcing just because it was written down.
evidence: VAMS-14 (constraint-block semantics via attribute instances) — tasks.md Open Item #5 said a task 'MUST be added before Phase 7 is considered closed' (process)
